title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the S_3-equivariant study of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} (U_{0,3}) over Q-bar, with its abelianised profinite fundamental group, the 'Fermat tower'. M^ = M-hat = pi_1(U_{0,3,Qbar})^ab is the Tate-twisted H_1, roughly Z-hat^2 = (Z-hat^3 / diagonal)(1). It carries the natural action of Z-hat^* (cyclotomic character) and of S_3 (permutation of the three cusps).

(234) S_3 acts on U_{0,3} but fixes no point. One therefore uses the S_3-equivariant fundamental group, i.e. pi_1 of the orbifold quotient [U_{0,3}/S_3]. This gives an extension of S_3 by the geometric pi_1 (based at some S_3-stable datum, written -J).

(233) Pushing (234) out along the commutator quotient pi_1 -> pi_1^ab gives an extension 1 -> M^ -> E -> S_3 -> 1.

Triviality of (233):
- Grothendieck first asserts that (233) is NOT split, although its restrictions to {1,rho,rho^2} = Z/3 and to {1,sigma} split. Those restrictions split because rho and sigma have fixed points on U_{0,3}: the primitive 6th roots of unity for rho, and -1, 1/2, 2 for the transpositions.
- From this he deduces that (232) is a fortiori nontrivial. (232) is the larger extension of Z-hat^* x S_3 by M^, coming from the arithmetic group G_{rho,sigma}/mu; it has canonical splittings over Z-hat, Z/3 and Z/2.
- A later marginal note corrects this: 'si, elle est triviale, cf plus bas'.
- The correction is right. H^2(S_3, M^) is killed by 6 and injects into the product of its restrictions to the Sylow subgroups Z/2 and Z/3. Splitting over both Sylows therefore forces the class to vanish.

(235)/(236) With (233) split, G_{rho,sigma}/mu can be realised inside the affine group Aff_{Z-hat}(M^) = Aut(M^) . M^, namely in the subgroup Aff = (Z-hat^* x S_3) semidirect M^. This gives the exact row (237), 1 -> M^ -> Aff -> Z-hat^* x S_3 -> 1. Its quotient receives a map from the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{0,3} (in effect Gal(Qbar/Q) x S_3, via the cyclotomic character times the identity).

Claim continued on the next page:
- The 'structure (230)', i.e. the Fermat tower with its Galois and S_3 operations, is equivalent (up to non-unique isomorphism) to an M^-conjugacy class of lifts M_{0,3} -> Aff of the map M_{0,3} -> Z-hat^* x S_3.
- Changing the base point translates by an element x of M^, which conjugates the lift.
- Grothendieck then proposes comparing these lifts with the canonical homomorphisms (217)/(218) into G_{rho,sigma}/mu.

In modern terms: this is the Galois action on the first metabelian layer pi/pi', the abelian (Fermat) level of the Galois action on pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points. It is encoded as a nonabelian H^1-type datum, a conjugacy class of affine lifts, made S_3-equivariant.
errors: The main-text claim that (233) is a nontrivial extension is wrong. The splittings over the Sylow subgroups Z/3 and Z/2 force H^2(S_3, M^) to vanish on this class, since restriction to Sylows is injective on the p-primary parts. Grothendieck himself corrects this in the margin ('si, elle est triviale, cf plus bas').
The 'a fortiori' deduction that (232) is nontrivial therefore collapses as well; the text goes on to embed the group in the split group Aff, consistent with the correction.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} and its abelianised extension of S_3 by M^
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the quotient stack [M_{0,3}/S_3] (equivalently M_{0,[3]}); equivariant pi_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche); later Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps on S_3 symmetry of GT
ideas.where_published: Themes of S_3 symmetry and tangential base points appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific extension is unsure

ideas.what: Triviality of an extension of a finite group detected by restriction to Sylow subgroups (fixed points of rho and sigma give the local splittings)
ideas.modern_name: Sylow restriction injectivity in group cohomology

ideas.what: Encoding the Galois/S_3 action on the Fermat tower (the maximal abelian cover of P^1 minus 3 points) as an M^-conjugacy class of lifts of Gal x S_3 -> Z-hat^* x S_3 into the affine group (Z-hat^* x S_3) semidirect M^, with base-point change acting by translation and conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the metabelian quotient pi/pi' (Fermat curves, Jacobi sums); affine/Kummer cocycle of a base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson (1989, hyperadelic gamma), Coleman, Deligne (1989)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, apparently independently of and possibly before Ihara and Anderson, the program of describing the Galois action on the Fermat tower S_3-equivariantly. He does so via affine lifts into (Z-hat^* x S_3) semidirect M^, and plans to compare them with canonical homomorphisms (217)/(218) into an arithmetic group G_{rho,sigma}/mu. This is historical priority interest rather than new mathematics, since Ihara and Anderson went much further (power series and Jacobi sums, the hyperadelic gamma function).
missed.quote: La donnée de la structure (230) équivaut, à isom (non unique) près, à la donnée d'une classe de M̂-conjugaison de relèvements
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents Grothendieck's own route into the metabelian Galois representation (Fermat tower) within the Longue Marche, relevant to the history of anabelian geometry and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard. The noteworthy points are a self-corrected error, fixed by a Sylow argument, and an early S_3-equivariant formulation of the Fermat-tower Galois action that anticipates Ihara and Anderson, without results beyond them.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Cette structure d'extension (233) ... n'est pas triviale, nous avons bien que l'extension induite...' probably reads '... n'est pas triviale, bien que l'extension induite ... le soit'.
'Dans ce sous-cas de vérifier ce point tantôt...)' is probably '(nous risquons de vérifier ce point tantôt...)' or similar. It is a parenthetical, not 'sous-cas'.
The marginal note 'si, elle est triviale, cf plus bas...' sits in the left margin next to the claim of non-triviality; it is a later correction.
'Le groupe G_{ρ,σ}/μ_C ne peut s'identifier' more likely reads '... peut s'identifier', consistent with the following construction.
The label inserted under 'groupe' near Aff_Ẑ(M̂) ≃ Aut_Ẑ(M̂).M̂ is most likely '(236)', since the equation numbers run 234, 235, [236], 237, and not '(234)'.
In the diagram (237) the source of the diagonal arrow is written M_{0,3} (script M), i.e. the arithmetic pi_1 of the moduli stack, not U_{0,3}.
